biography:
Throbbing Gristle were an English music and visual arts group formed in 1976 in Kingston upon Hull by Genesis P-Orridge and Cosey Fanni Tutti, later joined by Peter "Sleazy" Christopherson and Chris Carter. Evolving from the experimental performance art group COUM Transmissions, the band emerged from London's avant-garde scene after the group relocated from Hull in 1973. The four members built a recording studio in Hackney dubbed "The Death Factory" and began performing music together, making their public debut in October 1976 at the COUM exhibition Prostitution. They released their debut single "United/Zyklon B Zombie" and debut album The Second Annual Report in 1977, establishing themselves as pioneers of industrial music by completely dissolving conventional song structures and introducing noise generators and oscillators as primary compositional tools.

Throughout their initial run from 1976 to 1981, Throbbing Gristle released several influential albums that challenged their contemporaries, including their third and final proper album 20 Jazz Funk Greats in 1979, recorded entirely in a studio for the first time. Influenced by avant-garde composers like Karlheinz Stockhausen and bands such as the Velvet Underground, the group's abrasive, aggressive sound explored themes of death, mutilation, and degradation while inspiring subsequent acts like Cabaret Voltaire, SPK, and Einstürzende Neubauten. The band performed their final show on May 29, 1981, at the Kezar Pavilion in San Francisco, announcing their dissolution shortly after.

After disbanding, the members pursued influential solo and collaborative projects: Genesis P-Orridge co-founded Psychic TV and later Coil, while Cosey Fanni Tutti and Chris Carter formed the synthpop outfit Chris & Cosey. Throbbing Gristle reunited in 2004 and released three additional albums before disbanding again in 2010 following Peter Christopherson's death. Their legacy as equal parts performance art and pure noise remains foundational to industrial music and experimental music practice.

perplexity.biography:
Throbbing Gristle were an English music and visual arts group formed in 1976 in Kingston upon Hull by Genesis P-Orridge and Cosey Fanni Tutti, later joined by Peter "Sleazy" Christopherson and Chris Carter. Evolving from the experimental performance art group COUM Transmissions, the band emerged from London's avant-garde scene after the group relocated from Hull in 1973. The four members built a recording studio in Hackney dubbed "The Death Factory" and began performing music together, making their public debut in October 1976 at the COUM exhibition Prostitution. They released their debut single "United/Zyklon B Zombie" and debut album The Second Annual Report in 1977, establishing themselves as pioneers of industrial music by completely dissolving conventional song structures and introducing noise generators and oscillators as primary compositional tools.

Throughout their initial run from 1976 to 1981, Throbbing Gristle released several influential albums that challenged their contemporaries, including their third and final proper album 20 Jazz Funk Greats in 1979, recorded entirely in a studio for the first time. Influenced by avant-garde composers like Karlheinz Stockhausen and bands such as the Velvet Underground, the group's abrasive, aggressive sound explored themes of death, mutilation, and degradation while inspiring subsequent acts like Cabaret Voltaire, SPK, and Einstürzende Neubauten. The band performed their final show on May 29, 1981, at the Kezar Pavilion in San Francisco, announcing their dissolution shortly after.

After disbanding, the members pursued influential solo and collaborative projects: Genesis P-Orridge co-founded Psychic TV and later Coil, while Cosey Fanni Tutti and Chris Carter formed the synthpop outfit Chris & Cosey. Throbbing Gristle reunited in 2004 and released three additional albums before disbanding again in 2010 following Peter Christopherson's death. Their legacy as equal parts performance art and pure noise remains foundational to industrial music and experimental music practice.
